Here's my JS: function ClearPage() // unloads every page { document.getElementById('home').style.display = 'none'; document.getElementById('menu').style.display = 'none'; document.getElementById('teasers').style.display = 'none'; document.getElementById('nopage').style.display = 'none'; } function SetPage(page) // loads specified page { ClearPage(); if (document.getElementById(page)) document.getElementById(page).style.display = 'block'; else document.getElementById('nopage').style.display = 'block'; } // Called on hash change - calls SetPage and passes in whatever page is in the hash function UpdatePage() { window.scrollTo(0, 0); const hash = window.location.hash; if (hash.substring(1) == '') SetPage('home'); else SetPage(hash.substring(1)); } and the relevant HTML:

The CSS for #container: #container { min-height: calc(100vh - var(--container-sub)); max-height: fit-content; padding-left: 10px; font-family: 'Press Start 2P'; } #container h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6 { margin-top: 0px; padding-top: 18px; color: rgba(255, 145, 0, 1); } When clicking on the nav button for "Menu" (the page with the longest content), the view scrolls to the bottom of the page. It doesn't happen for the top section, #home, so i can only assume it's to do with the positioning of the sections though I wouldn't know how to go about fixing that. I tried using window.scroll(0, 0); in UpdatePage() , but it occasionally caused a flicker, and didn't affect anything if you clicked "menu" while you were already on that page.
